Let <MATH_0001> be a finite morphism. Then <MATH_0002> is
a quasi-coherent <MATH_0003>-module
(Lemma <REF_0001>)
of finite type
(by our definition of finite morphisms and
Properties, Lemma <REF_0002>).
We claim there is a closed immersion
<MATH_0004>
over <MATH_0005>, which finishes
the proof. Namely, we let <MATH_0006> be the morphism which corresponds
(via Constructions, Lemma <REF_0003>)
to the surjection
<MATH_0007>
coming from the adjunction map <MATH_0008>. Then <MATH_0009>
is a closed immersion. Namely, affine locally on <MATH_0010> we can write
<MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012>. Since <MATH_0013> is finite over <MATH_0014>
we may choose <MATH_0015> generating <MATH_0016> as an <MATH_0017>-module.
Then the <MATH_0018>-algebra map <MATH_0019>
sending <MATH_0020> to <MATH_0021> and <MATH_0022> to <MATH_0023> for <MATH_0024> is surjective.
Whence <MATH_0025> is a closed subscheme of
<MATH_0026> by Constructions, Lemma
<REF_0004>.
Thus it suffices to prove that the induced morphism
<MATH_0027> is a closed immersion
(see for example, Lemma <REF_0005>).
The reader checks that <MATH_0028> has image contained
in the open <MATH_0029> and that <MATH_0030>
corresponds to the surjective <MATH_0031>-algebra map
<MATH_0032> sending <MATH_0033> to <MATH_0034>.
Whence <MATH_0035> is an immersion (as a composition
of a closed immersion and an open immersion). Since
<MATH_0036> is finite over <MATH_0037> the image of this immersion is closed
(this uses Lemma <REF_0006>,
Lemma <REF_0007>, and
Constructions, Lemma <REF_0008>).
We conclude by Schemes, Lemma <REF_0009>.
